content:
據《金融時報》報道，最新嘅法院文件顯示，OpenAI 對透過 Apple Intelligence 推廣 ChatGPT 嘅進度感到失望，認為其表現「遠低於預期」，呢種情況係喺 2024 年推出後開始浮現。詳情如下。

OpenAI is asking the court to rule before trial

In August 2025, Musk said that X, which has been merged into SpaceXAI, would sue Apple and OpenAI over allegations of conspiring to suppress AI industry competitors. The lawsuit stems from a deal between OpenAI and Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

After the case was formally filed, the scope of the lawsuit has actually gone beyond the App Store ranking issues Musk publicly complained about. X and SpaceXAI also accuse Apple of trying to suppress the development of "super apps," including X's efforts to build an "everything app."

In the weeks and months that followed, the involved companies filed briefs, allegations, and rebuttals with the court. Apple and OpenAI have repeatedly argued that the agreement is not the exclusive partnership alleged in the lawsuit; court documents filed during the same period also revealed new details about how the two sides' collaboration operates.

One such detail was disclosed in a filing OpenAI submitted today. According to the Financial Times, OpenAI "expressed disappointment at the low interest from iPhone users in the 'Apple Intelligence' ChatGPT feature," a situation that emerged after the agreement was reached in 2024.

The report states:

Court documents unsealed Wednesday show that when the deal was reached in 2024, OpenAI had originally expected the promotional and branding collaboration with Apple to produce a "halo effect" and had projected gaining more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. However, less than a month after the ChatGPT integration feature launched, performance saw a "slow start," and OpenAI immediately revised down its weekly active user growth forecast. The documents indicate that by summer 2025, "it was already clearly apparent that Apple's integration of ChatGPT had performed significantly below expectations."

The report notes that several passages of dialogue in today's filing have been redacted, but the unredacted portions show that OpenAI executives were concerned Apple might "want to move faster" to find another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Federighi said in an interview that the company ultimately hopes to let users choose among different AI models, specifically mentioning that Google Gemini could potentially be one of the integrated options in the future.

That particular collaboration ultimately did not materialise, but Apple later adopted Google's Gemini model to power the new Siri AI; Xcode has also expanded support for coding agent tools from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI.

Returning to today's filing, the Financial Times mentioned that the documents also point out that the way Apple implemented ChatGPT may be one reason for the low adoption rate, because the relevant integration feature is off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also arguing that SpaceX's recent securities disclosure documents undermine SpaceXAI's claim that its partnership with Apple harms competition. OpenAI stated in the filing that SpaceX's IPO registration statement is full of disclosures that are "the exact opposite" of the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit.

Based on all of the above, OpenAI is asking Judge Pittman (Mark Pittman) to rule in favour of OpenAI on SpaceXAI's antitrust allegations before trial. The case is currently scheduled to go to trial in January.

Readers can find related reports in the Financial Times and Reuters coverage.
